subtopic: A power cut or rain spoils plans
subtype: Approach: finishing homework before the battery dies [Action]
passage: The storm warning crackled from the radio. "Ma, a storm is coming tonight," Sameer said, pulling the laptop closer. "So?" said his mother Sudha, stirring the dal. "So the online maths task is due tomorrow, and if the power goes, I lose it. I am doing it now." Forty minutes later he clicked Submit. "Done. Now I need the printer." "For what?" "The science notes. If there is no charge tomorrow, I still have paper." Sudha raised an eyebrow. "Since when do you plan like this?" Sameer grinned. "Since last time." At nine the lights went out. Warm under a blanket, Sameer read the printed pages by torchlight.

qa.q: What did Sameer print before the storm?
Why did Sameer decide to finish the online task early, and what was he worried about?
qa.a: He worried that a power cut would make him miss the deadline, so he wanted the task safely submitted.

qa.q: What other step could Sameer take against an outage, and why?
qa.a: He could charge the phone and laptop fully and keep a torch nearby, because he can keep working or reading if the lights go.

qa.q: How might Sudha feel seeing Sameer plan this well?
qa.a: Surprised and pleased, since she raised an eyebrow and asked since when he plans like this. 🙂

grounding: A boy finishes an online task early and prints notes before a storm, so a power cut cannot strand him.

subtopic: A power cut or rain spoils plans
subtype: Approach: finishing homework before the battery dies [Action]
passage: Last July our class had an online science quiz due on Friday night. I'm Jomon. On Wednesday evening the weather bulletin said a big storm would reach our district on Thursday. I remembered the last storm: no power for a whole day and no internet for two. My friend Divyansh said, "There's still Friday." But I thought, what if there isn't? So on Wednesday night I did the quiz, all twenty questions, and submitted it. Then I printed the notes for the next chapter at the shop downstairs, in case the lights went. The storm came on Thursday afternoon. The power was off till Saturday. On Monday half the class had missed the quiz. Mine was already marked.

qa.q: How did Jomon likely feel on Monday?
qa.a: Relieved, and probably proud of having finished before the storm.

qa.q: What else could Jomon do when a storm is forecast?
qa.a: Charge devices early and tell the teacher in advance if work might not reach on time.

qa.q: What would change if Jomon had waited for Friday, as Divyansh suggested?
qa.a: With the power off until Saturday, Jomon would likely have missed the quiz like half the class.

grounding: Looking back, a child hears a storm forecast, finishes online work early and prints notes so an outage cannot block the deadline.

passage:
Class 6 teacher's note, after the cyclone warning.
On Tuesday the weather office warned that a cyclone would reach our coast on Thursday. The class project was due online on Friday. On Wednesday morning Zubin came to me with a printed copy of his project and a question: "I've uploaded it already. Can I also give you this, in case the internet goes?" He had finished it on Tuesday night, three days early, and printed his revision notes at the stationery shop too. The cyclone cut power to most of the town for two days. On Monday, eleven students asked for extensions. Zubin's work was already marked. I have shared his idea with the class: when a storm is forecast, finish early and keep a paper copy.
Minakshi, class teacher

qa.q: How many students asked for extensions?
What might Zubin have been thinking when he brought the printed copy?
qa.a: He was worried the internet might fail and wanted to be safe, careful and prepared.

qa.q: What else could students do when a storm is forecast?
qa.a: Charge devices, keep paper copies, and tell the teacher early if they may not be able to submit.

qa.q: How does Minakshi see Zubin's idea?
qa.a: Minakshi finds it useful enough to share with the whole class.

grounding: A teacher's note records a boy finishing online work early and printing it when a storm is forecast, avoiding the outage.
